Refinement was performed using a layered–type structure (space group R-3m). The background was modeled using a polynomial, and peak profiles were fitted with a pseudo-Voigt function to account for instrumental broadening. Scale factor, lattice parameters, zero shift, and peak shape parameters were refined sequentially, followed by refinement of atomic positions and site occupancies.

Solid lines overlaid on the experimental data represent fitted component peaks obtained using CasaXPS software. figures.label: S6
figures.caption: Supplementary Fig. 6. Schematic illustration of the proposed interfacial interaction mechanism between VGCF and PTFE. Before shear mixing (A), surface oxygen functional groups on VGCF are predominantly in the enol form (C-OH). After shear mixing with PTFE (B), these groups undergo an enol-to-keto transition to form C=O species, promoting chemical coupling between VGCF and the fibrillated PTFE binder.

figures.label: S13
figures.caption: Supplementary Fig. 13. Relative effective diffusivity of Li+ as a function of tortuosity factor for slurry-processed and dry-processed thick electrodes. The effective diffusivity was calculated by combining the measured porosity and tortuosity obtained from segmented PFIB-SEM reconstructions, assuming identical intrinsic electrolyte diffusivity in both electrodes. The dry- processed electrode exhibits a higher effective Li⁺ diffusivity, reflecting reduced tortuosity and more efficient ionic transport pathways through the electrolyte phase.

figures.label: S14
figures.caption: Supplementary Fig. 14. LSV measurements of the dry-processed and slurry-processed carbon and binder composite until 4.8 V versus Li metal anode. Note the 3.9 V oxidation peak for slurry- processed sample is attributed to early-onset Al current collector corrosion and electrolyte reactions. As reported,16 Al foils in LiPF6–carbonate electrolytes begin to undergo pitting corrosion just above ~3.8–4.0 V. In our slurry-cast PTFE/PVDF control sample (which contains no active material), the film is relatively sparse — increasing the likelihood of local pinholes that expose bare Al directly to electrolyte, thereby triggering this Al–electrolyte reaction around 3.9 V.
